findings.issue_text: src/sentry/api/paginator.py:840 — P1, confidence 100: `return int(math.floor(value) if self._is_asc(for_prev) else math.ceil(value))` gives the new paginator a numeric key contract although its only endpoint selects `order_by="-datetime"`, so every nonempty optimized audit-log page fails to encode its datetime keys and existing millisecond cursors also lose DateTimePaginator's timestamp decoding through `return cursor.value`; retain the datetime codec when introducing an audit-log paginator.

src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:70 — P1, confidence 100: `use_optimized = request.GET.get("optimized_pagination") == "true"` replaces the entire date-filtering block without relocating it, so both pagination branches ignore previously supported `start`, `end`, and `statsPeriod` constraints and return audit entries outside the requested interval, breaking the endpoint's filtering contract even when optimization is disabled.

src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:70 — P1, confidence 100: `use_optimized = request.GET.get("optimized_pagination") == "true"` replaces the existing date-filtering block without restoring its behavior in either pagination branch, so requests supplying `start`/`end` or `statsPeriod` now return audit entries outside the requested period even when optimized pagination is disabled.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:840 — [P1, confidence 100] `return int(math.floor(value) if self._is_asc(for_prev) else math.ceil(value))` passes an audit entry's `datetime` to numeric rounding because the endpoint selects this paginator with `order_by="-datetime"`, raising `TypeError: must be real number, not datetime.datetime` when generating cursors for every nonempty optimized first page, as reproduced by executing the actual class definitions with a datetime-valued row.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:882 — [P1, confidence 75] `results = list(queryset[start_offset:stop])` uses the negative `cursor.offset` assigned at line 880 when advanced features are enabled, but Django QuerySet rejects negative slice bounds, so the advertised negative-offset pagination path raises an exception before retrieving any audit logs; rebuttal requires a concrete queryset implementation in this endpoint that supports negative slicing.

src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:70 — P1, confidence 100: Replacing `queryset = queryset.filter(datetime__range=(start, end))` with `use_optimized = request.GET.get("optimized_pagination") == "true"` removes the existing date-range restriction from both pagination paths, so requests specifying `start`/`end` or `statsPeriod` silently return audit entries outside the requested interval, changing audit-query semantics under a pagination-performance objective without recorded human acceptance of removing date filtering.

src/sentry/api/paginator.py:840 — P1, confidence 100: `return int(math.floor(value) if self._is_asc(for_prev) else math.ceil(value))` works for an empty audit queryset but raises `TypeError: must be real number, not datetime.datetime` when an authorized optimized request returns its first audit entry, because the endpoint orders by `-datetime` and `build_cursor` calls this key function before serialization, leaving the request failed instead of returning rows; the strongest rebuttal is that pagination is optional and empty results succeed, but neither protects an administrator enabling the feature on a populated organization, and the existing DateTimePaginator explicitly converts datetime values before rounding.

src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:68 — P1, confidence 100: Replacing the existing date-filtering block with `use_optimized = request.GET.get("optimized_pagination") == "true"` removes `queryset = queryset.filter(datetime__range=(start, end))` from both pagination paths, so existing `start`/`end` and `statsPeriod` requests now include audit entries outside their requested interval even without opting into optimized pagination, an unrelated API behavior regression outside the stated pagination-performance scope.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a bug in the new OptimizedCursorPaginator class. Looking at line 840 in the diff, `get_item_key` does `value = getattr(item, self.key)` and then `return int(math.floor(value) if self._is_asc(for_prev) else math.ceil(value))`. The endpoint orders by `-datetime`, so `self.key` would be 'datetime'. When `getattr(item, 'datetime')` returns a datetime object, calling `math.floor()` or `math.ceil()` on it will raise `TypeError: must be real number, not datetime.datetime`. The existing DateTimePaginator (visible in the codebase context) handles datetime conversion properly, but this new OptimizedCursorPaginator does not. This is a real bug that would cause failures when the paginator is used with datetime fields.
